evidence.excerpt: This paper investigates whether DMA measurements—specifically storage modulus E′, loss modulus E″, and the loss tangent tan δ recorded at 1, 10, and 100 Hz—can serve as rapid non-destructive predictors of residual fatigue life in humidity-aged polymer specimens without performing full fatigue tests. Four materials were studied: PA6, PA66-GF30, POM-C, and PEEK, each aged at 85% RH and 37 °C for 0, 4, 8, 16, and 32 weeks. DMA signatures were correlated with fatigue lives measured at a fixed stress amplitude of 40% of the tensile strength for each material–ageing combination (n = 8 per data point). For PA6 and PA66-GF30, tan δ at 1 Hz showed the strongest correlation with residual fatigue life (Pearson r = −0.91 and −0.87 respectively). POM-C and PEEK showed weaker correlations (r = −0.61 and −0.54), consistent with their low moisture uptake limiting the DMA-detectable change. A simple regression-based screening criterion using tan δ thresholds is proposed and its applicability limits are discussed.
